{{nihongo|'''Sogahime Shrine'''|蘇我比咩神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shimōsa Province]].

'''Sogahime Shrine''' (そがひめじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Soga 2-chōme, {{ill|Chūō-ku, Chiba|Q1075869|qid=Q1075869|lt=Chūō Ward}}, {{ill|Chiba (city)|Q170616|qid=Q170616}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|Q80011|qid=Q80011}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

The principal enshrined deities are Sogahime Ōkami and Chiyoharu Inari Ōkami. Also enshrined are {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, the {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|Q11088805|qid=Q11088805}} ({{ill|Futsunushi|fr|Futsunushi|it|Futsunushi|ja|経津主神|mni|ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯨꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Futsunushi|ru|Фуцунуси|zh|經津主神|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsunushi no Kami}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|lt=Takemikazuchi|Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi no Kami}}, {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane no Kami}}, and {{ill|Himegami|Q22070227|qid=Q22070227|lt=Ame-no-Koyane Himegami}}), and {{ill|Hachiman|ar|هاتشيمان|az|Haçiman|ca|Hachiman|de|Hachiman|el|Χατσίμαν|es|Hachiman|eu|Hachiman|fa|هاچیمان|fi|Hachiman|fr|Hachiman|hu|Hacsiman|id|Hachiman|it|Hachiman|ja|八幡神|ko|하치만 신|mni|ꯍꯆꯤꯃꯥꯟ|my|ဟချိမန်း|pl|Hachiman|pt|Hachiman|ru|Хатиман|simple|Hachiman|sl|Hačiman|sv|Hachiman|tok|jan sewi Kasiman|tr|Hachiman|uk|Хачіман|uz|Hachiman|vi|Hachiman|wuu|八幡神|zh|八幡神|qid=Q261637}} ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}, Hime Ōkami, and {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}). In the medieval period, the Kasuga deities became the center of worship, and the shrine was called Kasuga Daimyōjin.

=== History ===
The date of founding is unknown. According to the myths recorded in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, when {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru no Mikoto}} was on his eastern campaign and attempted to cross from Sagami to Fusa Province, he encountered a violent storm. To calm it, his consort {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Oto Tachibana-hime}} threw herself into the sea. According to shrine tradition, five women who had accompanied Oto Tachibana-hime also entered the water with her. Of these, only Sogahime, the daughter of a Soga minister, was washed ashore, where she was cared for by villagers, revived, and returned to the capital. Later, when the villagers heard that Yamato Takeru had died on his way back, they built a shrine to console his spirit. {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}} was deeply moved by this act and appointed the {{ill|Soga clan|Q909854|qid=Q909854}} as {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|Q2483673|qid=Q2483673}} of the surrounding area. The Soga clan revered {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|Q714559|qid=Q714559}} and Hime Shrine, and it is said that they invited the deities of both shrines and founded Sogahime Shrine.

However, there is another tradition: it was Oto Tachibana-hime herself who was washed ashore and revived, and because she said “I have revived (yo-mi-gaeri),” the place name “Soga” is said to have originated from this phrase.

In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as “{{ill|Shimōsa Province|Q1053695|qid=Q1053695}}{{ill|Chiba District, Chiba|Q5095301|qid=Q5095301}} Sogahime Shrine,” and is ranked as a minor shrine.

In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 19 ({{ill|1613|Q6776|qid=Q6776}}), {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}} donated a shrine estate of 10 koku.
